chapter.li: LEChapter6 Verse1 Now I’m not providing my ancestors’ genealogy in this part of my record, and I’m not going to do so on these plates that I’m engraving since it’s provided in my father’s record; so it’s not included here. VerseEnd Verse2 I’m content to say that we’re descended from Joseph. VerseEnd Verse3 Moreover, I don’t care to provide a detailed account of all the events involving my father, since they won’t fit on these plates, because I need the space so I can write the things of God. VerseEnd Verse4 My whole intent is to persuade people to come to the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob and be saved. VerseEnd Verse5 Therefore I don’t write what’s pleasing to the world, but what’s pleasing to God and important for those who aren’t worldly. VerseEnd Verse6 And so I’ll command my descendants not to fill these plates with things that aren’t valuable to mankind. VerseEnd

LEChapter7 Verse1 Now I want 2PP you to know that after my father had finished prophesying about his descendants, the Lord spoke to him again, saying it wasn’t right for him to take his family into the wilderness alone, but that his sons were to marry suitable women so that they could raise up children to the Lord in the promised land. VerseEnd Verse2 The Lord commanded him that my brothers and I were to return to the land of Jerusalem and bring Ishmael and his family back across the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse3 So I went again with my brothers through the wilderness to go back up to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse4 We went to Ishmael’s house and gained his confidence, then we told him the Lord’s words. VerseEnd Verse5 And the Lord softened Ishmael’s heart and also his whole household’s, so that they went with us through the wilderness back down to our father’s tent. VerseEnd

Verse6 As we traveled in the wilderness, Laman, Lemuel, two of Ishmael’s daughters, and two of his sons and their families rebelled against me, Sam, their father Ishmael and his wife, and his three other daughters. VerseEnd Verse7 They rebelled because they wanted to return to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse8 Now I was troubled because of the hardness of their hearts, so I spoke to them, to Laman and Lemuel, saying: 2PP You are my older brothers. Why are 2PP you so hard in 2PP your hearts and blind in 2PP your minds that 2PP you need me, 2PP your younger brother, to speak to 2PP you and set an example for 2PP you? VerseEnd Verse9 Why haven’t 2PP you listened to the Lord’s word? VerseEnd Verse10 How can 2PP you forget 2PP you’ve seen an angel of the Lord? VerseEnd Verse11 How have 2PP you forgotten the great things the Lord has done for us, in rescuing us from Laban and letting us obtain the record? VerseEnd Verse12 And how have 2PP you forgotten the Lord can do everything for mankind according to His will, if they exercise faith in Him? So let’s be faithful to Him. VerseEnd Verse13 And if we’re faithful to Him, we’ll reach the promised land. At some time in the future, 2PP you’ll know the Lord’s word concerning Jerusalem’s destruction will be fulfilled, since everything the Lord has said about Jerusalem’s destruction is certain to happen. VerseEnd Verse14 The Spirit of the Lord will soon stop struggling with them, because they’ve rejected the prophets, thrown Jeremiah in prison, and tried to kill our father, driving him away. VerseEnd Verse15 Because of this, I tell 2PP you that if 2PP you choose to return to Jerusalem, 2PP you’ll die with them as well. Now, if 2PP you want to make that choice, go back up there. But remember the words I tell 2PP you, that if 2PP you go, 2PP you’re sure to lose 2PP your lives too. This is what the Spirit of the Lord compels me to say to 2PP you. VerseEnd

Verse16 When I said this to my brothers, they got angry with me. And they took me by force because they were extremely angry. They tied me up with ropes in order to leave me in the wilderness to be eaten by wild animals as their plan to kill me. VerseEnd Verse17 But I prayed to the Lord, saying: O Lord, according to my faith in 2PSI You, please free me from my brothers! Give me strength so I can break these ropes that have me tied. VerseEnd Verse18 When I said this, the ropes around my hands and feet came undone, and I stood in front of my brothers and spoke to them again. VerseEnd Verse19 And they got angry with me again and started to attack me. But one of Ishmael’s daughters and her mother and one of Ishmael’s sons pled with my brothers, and it softened their hearts and they gave up their determined efforts to kill me. VerseEnd Verse20 They regretted their wickedness, so they bowed down in front of me and begged me to forgive them for how they had treated me. VerseEnd Verse21 And I freely forgave them all they had done and urged them to pray to the Lord their God for forgiveness. And they did so. After they had finished praying to the Lord, we traveled back to our father’s tent. VerseEnd

Verse22 We went down to our father’s tent, and after my brothers and I and Ishmael’s family arrived at my father’s tent, they gave thanks to the Lord God and offered sacrifice and burnt offerings to Him. VerseEnd
LEChapter8 Verse1 And we had gathered all kinds of seeds: many kinds of both grains and fruit. VerseEnd

Verse2 While my father was there in the wilderness, he told us: I’ve had a dream, or in other words, I’ve seen a vision. VerseEnd Verse3 Because of what I’ve seen, I have reason to praise the Lord about Nephi, and about Sam as well. I have reason to think they will be saved along with many of their descendants. VerseEnd Verse4 But, Laman and Lemuel, I’m very concerned for 2PP you. Indeed, it seemed like I saw a dark and gloomy wilderness. VerseEnd Verse5 And I saw a man dressed in a white robe who stood before me. VerseEnd Verse6 He talked to me and said I should follow him. VerseEnd Verse7 As I followed him, I saw I was in a dark and dreary wasteland. VerseEnd Verse8 After I had traveled for many hours in darkness, I began to pray to the Lord to help me, because of His many tender mercies. VerseEnd

Verse9 After I had prayed to the Lord, I saw a large and spacious field. VerseEnd Verse10 Then I saw a tree with fruit that would make people happy. VerseEnd Verse11 I went and ate some of the fruit, discovering it was sweet beyond measure, better than all that I had ever tasted before. I noticed its fruit was white, brighter than I had ever seen. VerseEnd

Verse12 As I ate the fruit, it made my soul very joyful. So I began to wish my family would eat some of it too, since I knew it was better than all other fruit. VerseEnd Verse13 As I looked around, trying to catch sight of my family, I saw a river. It ran beside the tree whose fruit I was eating. VerseEnd Verse14 I looked to see where it came from and saw its source a little way off. At its source I saw 2PP your mother Sariah, Sam, and Nephi, standing there and looking lost. VerseEnd Verse15 I waved to them and yelled for them to come over to me and eat some of the fruit, which was better than any other fruit. VerseEnd Verse16 And they came over to me and also ate the fruit. VerseEnd Verse17 And I wanted Laman and Lemuel to come and eat some of the fruit too. Therefore I looked toward the source of the river to try to locate them. VerseEnd Verse18 I saw them, but they refused to come over to me and eat the fruit. VerseEnd

Verse19 Then I saw an iron railing extending along the riverbank, leading to the tree next to me. VerseEnd Verse20 I also saw a straight and narrow path that ran along the iron railing all the way to the tree beside me. It also led by the source of the river to a large and spacious field, as big as the earth itself. VerseEnd Verse21 And I saw innumerable throngs of people, many of them pressing forward so they could reach the path that led to the tree I was standing next to. VerseEnd Verse22 They moved forward and started on the path leading to the tree. VerseEnd Verse23 Then a great dark cloud came up and those who had started on the path lost their way, wandering off and becoming lost. VerseEnd Verse24 And I saw others pressing forward. They came and caught hold of the end of the iron railing and moved forward through the dark clouds, clinging to the iron railing until they arrived and ate some of the fruit from the tree. VerseEnd Verse25 After they had eaten fruit from the tree, they looked around as if ashamed. VerseEnd

Verse26 I also looked around and saw on the other side of the river an impressive and large building. It stood like it was in the air, high above the earth, VerseEnd Verse27 and it was filled with people — old and young, male and female — and they wore expensive clothing. They appeared to mock and point their fingers at those who had come up and were eating the fruit. VerseEnd Verse28 Those who had tasted the fruit were ashamed because of people scoffing at them, and they left, following forbidden paths and were lost. VerseEnd

Verse29 Now I don’t write all my father’s words. VerseEnd Verse30 But to summarize, he saw other crowds coming forward. People came, grasped the end of the iron railing, and moved forward, continually holding firmly to the iron railing until they arrived, sat down, and ate some of the fruit from the tree. VerseEnd Verse31 He also saw other crowds of people moving toward that impressive and large building. VerseEnd Verse32 And many drowned in the deep river, and many disappeared from his view, wandering on unfamiliar roads. VerseEnd Verse33 A large number of people entered the large building. After they entered the building, they pointed at and made fun of me, and those who were also eating the fruit, but we didn’t pay attention to them. VerseEnd Verse34 My father said the following: All those who paid attention to the insults fell away. VerseEnd Verse35 And my father said that Laman and Lemuel didn’t eat any of the fruit. VerseEnd

Verse36 After my father had recounted everything about his dream or vision — and there was a lot covered — he told us that because of what he had seen in the vision, he was very afraid for Laman and Lemuel; afraid they would be shut out from the Lord’s presence. VerseEnd Verse37 He then urged them with all the feeling of a loving parent to listen to his words, because then the Lord might be merciful to them and not reject them. My father sincerely preached to them. VerseEnd Verse38 After he had preached and prophesied to them about many things, he pleaded with them to keep the Lord’s commandments. Then he finished speaking to them. VerseEnd LEChapter9 Verse1 My father saw, heard, and said all these things as he occupied a tent in the valley of Lemuel, and much more that can’t be written on these plates. VerseEnd

Verse2 Since I’ve mentioned these plates, these aren’t the ones on which I’m making a complete account of my people’s history. The plates set aside for that purpose I’ve given the name of Nephi; so they’re called the plates of Nephi after my own name. Well, these plates are also called the plates of Nephi. VerseEnd Verse3 Understand, the Lord commanded me to make these plates for the specific purpose of making a written account of my people’s ministry. VerseEnd Verse4 On the other plates there’s a written account of the kings’ rule and my people’s wars and in-fighting. So these plates focus on telling 2PP you about our ministry, and the other plates focus on the kings’ rule and my people’s wars and arguments. VerseEnd Verse5 I trust the Lord commanded me to make these plates for His wise purposes, but I can’t tell 2PP you His reasons. VerseEnd Verse6 2PP You see, the Lord knows all things from the beginning. Therefore He prepares in advance any needed response to accomplish all His plans for mankind, to fulfill all His words. That’s exactly how He works. Amen. VerseEnd
